en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect, symmetrical cone shape.
Taal Lake in Batangas sits inside a large volcanic caldera formed by massive prehistoric eruptions.
The sand at Pink Beach in Zamboanga gets its unique color from tiny red marine organisms.
The amihan brings cool, dry northeast monsoon winds to the Philippines between November and February.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol turn brown during the dry season, resembling giant chocolate mounds.
Callao Cave in Cagayan contains limestone stalactites that slowly drip water from the cave ceiling.
The Philippine tarsier in Bohol has enormous eyes that are each larger than its brain.
The Rafflesia, found in Luzon rainforests, blooms with the largest individual flower on Earth.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea features vertical coral walls dropping into deep trenches.
Mount Apo in Mindanao features mossy forests where tree trunks are covered in thick, wet moss.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River flows directly from a limestone cave into the South China Sea.
The Narra tree, the Philippine national tree, drops its small yellow flowers during the early summer.
